evidence.description: The initializer launches an unstructured Task to call an async method (retrieveStoredCredentials) without any way to manage, cancel, or await its completion.

candidates.explanation: Launching an unstructured Task in an initializer can lead to race conditions where the object's state is modified before initialization is complete, and it provides no mechanism for the caller to handle errors or ensure the task finishes before other operations begin.
candidates.title: Unstructured Task in Initializer

evidence.description: The userProfile property uses a didSet with a Task to post a notification on the MainActor.

candidates.explanation: Using a Task inside a didSet to perform side effects (like posting notifications) can lead to non-deterministic execution order and makes it difficult to reason about the state of the UI relative to the state of the actor.
candidates.title: Implicit Task Creation in Property Observer

evidence.description: The setupTokensWithCredentials method uses an unstructured Task to dispatch state changes.

candidates.explanation: The use of an unstructured Task to dispatch state changes means that the state management system might be updated out of order if multiple credential updates occur in rapid succession, as there is no guarantee of execution order for these tasks.
candidates.title: Unstructured Task for State Dispatch

evidence.description: The retrieveSSOCredentials method uses a conditional downcast (as?) to check for a specific provider type.

candidates.explanation: Using conditional downcasting to check for specific implementations (NativeToWebSSOAuth0Provider) violates the Dependency Inversion Principle and makes the service tightly coupled to a specific concrete implementation rather than an abstraction.
candidates.title: Type Checking via Downcasting
